claims.text: Differential oxidizability of constituent elements governs oxidation resistance and long-term material integrity in multiprincipal-element high-temperature alloys.
Initial oxidation behavior in CoCrFeNiMn depends on atomic size and redox potential, with redox potential becoming dominant over time.
Elements with higher redox potentials and generally smaller atomic sizes preferentially oxidize first.
Preferential oxidation produces a nanocrystalline, adherent surface oxide.
The protective oxide scale reduces oxygen ingress into the bulk alloy.
Dynamic amorphization of near-surface grain-boundary regions occurs in single-phase CoCrFeMnNi.
Dynamically amorphized grain-boundary regions improve the barrier properties of the oxide layer.
Inverse Hall-Petch behavior and dynamic grain-boundary processes accommodate stress and maintain the oxide-scale/substrate interface.
The baseline is an equiatomic, single-phase CoCrFeNiMn alloy with a homogeneous solid-solution microstructure.
A controlled comparison should enrich or deplete high-redox-potential elements, such as Cr, while keeping temperature, oxygen environment, and mechanical loading identical.
The modified sample should have greater than 10% enrichment of a high-redox-potential element relative to the equiatomic baseline.
High-redox-potential-element enrichment will produce a thinner, more adherent, and compositionally stable oxide layer than the equiatomic baseline.
High-redox-potential-element enrichment will slow oxidation kinetics relative to the equiatomic baseline.
High-redox-potential-element enrichment will improve retention of creep and wear resistance during high-temperature oxidation.
CoCrFeMnNi can develop an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer associated with low friction and high wear resistance in an inert, ultra-high-vacuum environment.
The proposed behavior should hold at approximately 600–800 °C under controlled oxygen partial pressure and moderate mechanical loading.
Phase transformations or extensive microstructural coarsening may alter oxidation kinetics and mechanical responses outside the proposed range.
Atom probe tomography, TEM, and X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy can characterize oxidation-induced compositional and structural evolution in CoCrFeNiMn.
Failure of the enriched alloy to improve both oxide-scale characteristics and mechanical performance relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
